$comment: OMN-18629. THE PAIRS. A bare primitive, and the governed helper this
repository already ships that supersedes it.
Read by scripts/ci/governed_helper_gate.py, which is invoked by the
governed-helper-primitive pre-commit hook and by
.github/workflows/governed-helper-primitive-gate.yml. The same module runs
in both places, so a local verdict and a CI verdict cannot diverge.
JSON rather than YAML deliberately, matching omniclaude's
ticket_creation_policy.json: the checker sits on a fail-closed enforcement
path that runs in pre-commit, where the resolved interpreter may be a bare
system python. A missing third-party parser there would turn into a refusal
of every commit on the machine.
There is deliberately NO exemption entry -- no 'any', no wildcard, no
suppression annotation the checker honours at any severity. The class these
pairs describe produced four verified defects in one night; a sanctioned
spelling for it is a sanctioned incident. A pair that is WRONG is corrected
here, where the change is reviewable and a reviewer can see every call site
it affects at once.
Fields per pair:
id                       -- stable; the baseline keys on it
bare_pattern             -- the primitive to refuse
governed_helper          -- file:line of the correct form, so the refusal
can point at real code rather than at doctrine
governed_form            -- what to write instead, in one line
scope_globs              -- where the pair applies
exclude_globs            -- the helper's own file and its test; these
carry the bare form on purpose, in prose
governed_prefix_pattern  -- text before a match that means the call site
is ALREADY governed. It exists because the
governed form is sometimes a prefix of the
bare one: a positive control during the
OMN-18629 measurement found that the declared
interpreter invocation matched the bare
interpreter pattern, so the strip has to
happen before the verdict, not after
established_by           -- the ticket that established the helper
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. A fourth pair for the bare interpreter in
WORKFLOW scope was measured and ruled out. 109 invocations match there, of
which 33 target a script that imports a third-party module; but a workflow
step may have installed that module into the system interpreter, so the
predicate is not decidable from the invocation line. Shipping it would
produce roughly 33 findings of which an unknown fraction are false, which is
how a gate earns the reputation that gets it routed around. Shell scope has
no such escape -- a script runs wherever it runs -- and the OMN-18606 defect
sits in shell scope exactly.
OMN-18608. A bare `mkdir` lock released only by a trap on EXIT INT TERM
is leaked permanently by a SIGKILL, and a directory with nothing in it
cannot tell a live holder from a corpse. Measured on the workstation
2026-09-17: a session died at about 15:25Z holding a lock taken at
15:23Z; every tick for the next 35 minutes printed 'another
reconcile-host is running; nothing to do' and exited 0 while `ps` showed
no reconcile process anywhere on the host. The dispatch venv went
unreconciled for that whole window and only moved when the directory was
removed by hand.
pairs.governed_form: write the holder (pid + host + timestamp) INTO the lock and decide staleness from it, as scripts/reconcile-host.sh does; never a bare mkdir released only by a trap

$comment: OMN-18613. In kafka-python a bare `commit()` commits the consumer's
POSITION for each assigned partition -- past every record already
FETCHED, not past the one record processed. A poller that deliberately
processes the first record of a batch therefore marks its unprocessed
batch-mates as done. Measured 2026-09-17: one poll returned offsets 262
and 263 together; accepting 262 committed 264, past the still-buffered
263, which was then never executed and left no job record, no acceptance
line, no rejection line and no quarantine record.
Scoped to a receiver whose name contains 'consumer' on purpose. A bare
`conn.commit()` on a database connection is correct and common, and a
pattern that refused it would be wrong far more often than right.
pairs.governed_form: commit the record's own partition explicitly -- commit({TopicPartition(msg.topic, msg.partition): OffsetAndMetadata(msg.offset + 1, ...)}) -- so the commit is bounded by the record it is about

$comment: OMN-18606. A shell script invoking a repo-local Python file through a
bare interpreter runs it against whatever interpreter happens to be on
PATH, with the project environment absent. lane-census-refresh.yml
merged green and failed on every real run for exactly this reason.
Shell scope only. See the top-level comment for why workflow scope is
ruled out rather than merely unimplemented.
The pattern requires a `.py` TARGET. A bare `python3 -c` one-liner over
the standard library needs no project environment and is not a defect,
so refusing it would be noise.
pairs.governed_helper: the declared invocation for this repository is `uv run`; see .pre-commit-config.yaml, where every hook entry uses it
pairs.governed_form: uv run --frozen python <script>.py, so the project environment is the one the script runs in
